steps.text: Take Cefpodoxime 200 mg twice a day until it is gone (next 7 days)
Take Tamsulosin 0.4 mg once a day while the stent is in
Keep lisinopril on hold until your doctor says otherwise
See urology to plan stone treatment and stent removal. The stent cannot stay in forever (as scheduled)
Get your kidney function rechecked as directed
Check your blood sugar as your diabetes plan says
Drink plenty of water unless a doctor told you to limit fluids

medications.name: Cefpodoxime
medications.howOften: twice a day by mouth for 7 more days
medications.why: An antibiotic to finish treating the infection. Take every dose even if you feel better.

medications.name: Tamsulosin
medications.howOften: once a day by mouth while the stent is in place
medications.why: Relaxes the urine tube so the stent is more comfortable. Keep taking it unless urology tells you to stop.

medications.name: Acetaminophen
medications.howOften: as needed for mild pain or fever, within the daily limit your care team gave you

medications.name: Atorvastatin
medications.why: Lowers cholesterol to protect your heart.

medications.name: Home diabetes medications
medications.howOften: as on your final medication list

medications.name: Lisinopril
medications.why: On hold until your doctor rechecks your kidneys and blood pressure. Do not restart it on your own.

medications.name: NSAIDs
medications.why: Avoid pain relievers like ibuprofen. They can hurt your kidneys after this illness. Ask first.

followUps.why: Treat the stone and remove or exchange the stent
Recheck your kidney function and blood pressure, and decide about lisinopril

warnings.text: Confusion, fainting, severe weakness, or trouble breathing
Worsening pain in your side or belly
Vomiting that will not stop or you cannot keep your medicines down
Making much less urine than usual
Signs the blockage or infection is back
Questions about stent symptoms such as a frequent urge to urinate or mild discomfort
